  "markdown": "Custom Rules\n\n# Custom Rules\n\nCustom rules provide a powerful way to define project-specific and global behaviors and constraints for the Kilo Code AI agent. With custom rules, you can ensure consistent formatting, restrict access to sensitive files, enforce coding standards, and customize the AI's behavior for your specific project needs or across all projects.\n\n## Overview\n\nCustom rules allow you to create text-based instructions that all AI models will follow when interacting with your project. Kilo Code can use most of what you already have in Cursor, but it does **not** read `.cursor/skills/` or `.cursor/rules/` automatically. You need a small config layer and, for rules, a format tweak.

## Short answer

| Cursor | Kilo Code | What to do |
|--------|-----------|------------|
| `.cursor/skills/*/SKILL.md` | `.kilo/skills/*/SKILL.md` or `skills.paths` | Point Kilo at your existing skills folder, or copy/symlink |
| `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` | `instructions` in `kilo.jsonc` + `.kilo/rules/*.md` | Convert `.mdc` → plain Markdown; wire up in config |
| Always-on / glob rules | `AGENTS.md` + `kilo.jsonc` | Put stable policy in `AGENTS.md`; split conditional rules into separate files or custom agents |
| User-level Cursor rules/skills | `~/.config/kilo/kilo.jsonc`, `~/.kilo/skills/` | Re-home global guidance there |
| `.cursor/mcp.json` | `mcp` in `kilo.jsonc` | Schema migration (`${env:VAR}` → `{env:VAR}`) |

Your repo already has the right **skill shape** (e.g. `garden-voice/SKILL.md` with `name` + `description` frontmatter). It just has **no Kilo config yet** — no `AGENTS.md`, no `kilo.jsonc`.

---

## 1. Skills (easiest part)

Kilo uses the same Agent Skills format: one folder per skill, `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter.

**Option A — reference Cursor’s folder (least duplication):**

```jsonc
// kilo.jsonc (project root)
{
  "skills": {
    "paths": [".cursor/skills"]
  }
}
```

**Option B — canonical Kilo layout:**

```text
.kilo/skills/
  garden-voice/SKILL.md
  jorap-voice/SKILL.md
  ...
```

You can copy or symlink from `.cursor/skills/`.

Kilo also auto-loads `.agents/skills/` and `.claude/skills/` (with compatibility on), but **not** `.cursor/skills/` unless you add it via `skills.paths`.

After changes: start a new session or run `/reload`.

**Check:** ask Kilo “What skills do you have?” or “Do you have access to garden-voice?”

---

## 2. Rules (more work)

Cursor rules live as `.mdc` with metadata like `alwaysApply` and `globs`:

```1:5:.cursor/rules/ponytail.mdc
---
description: Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode. Always pick the simplest solution that works.
globs:
alwaysApply: true
---
```

Kilo rules are **plain Markdown files** listed in `kilo.jsonc`:

```jsonc
{
  "instructions": [
    ".kilo/rules/*.md"
  ]
}
```

Kilo does **not** understand Cursor’s `.mdc` frontmatter or `globs`/`alwaysApply` the same way. You need to:

1. Copy each rule body into `.kilo/rules/<name>.md` (drop the YAML, or turn `description` into a `#` heading).
2. For **always-on** rules (`alwaysApply: true`) — either include them in `instructions`, or distill them into root `AGENTS.md`.
3. For **glob-scoped** rules — split into separate files and rely on you invoking the right agent/mode, or use `.kilo/agents/*.md` for specialized personas with different permissions.

**Backward-compat note:** old `.kilocode/rules/` still works, but current docs prefer `kilo.jsonc` + `.kilo/rules/`.

---

## 3. Add a portable `AGENTS.md` layer

Kilo’s [Cursor migration guide](https://kilo.ai/articles/cursor-to-kilo-migration-guide) recommends:

- **`AGENTS.md`** — stable, cross-tool project policy (works in Cursor *and* Kilo)
- **`kilo.jsonc`** — Kilo-specific ops (permissions, MCP, rule paths, skill paths)
- **`.kilo/agents/*.md`** — specialized agents (review-only, docs writer, etc.)

Your `personal-context-management` skill already describes this split:

> “Cursor already shards this — `.cursor/rules/`, user rules, and skills *are* the LLM-optimized master prompt.”

For Kilo, the portable piece is **`AGENTS.md`** plus skills; Kilo-specific wiring goes in **`kilo.jsonc`**.

---

## 4. User-level (global) Cursor stuff

Cursor also loads:

- **User rules** (Cursor settings)
- **Global skills** (e.g. `~/.cursor/skills-cursor/`)

Kilo equivalents:

| Scope | Location |
|-------|----------|
| Global skills | `~/.kilo/skills/` |
| Global rules/instructions | `~/.config/kilo/kilo.jsonc` → `instructions` array |

Those do not migrate from Cursor automatically; copy the content over.

---

## 5. Suggested layout for this repo

```text
jorap.com/
├── AGENTS.md                 # portable always-on policy (new)
├── kilo.jsonc                # Kilo config (new)
├── .cursor/
│   ├── skills/               # keep for Cursor
│   └── rules/                # keep for Cursor
└── .kilo/
    └── rules/                # Kilo copies of .mdc bodies (or symlink)
```

Example starter `kilo.jsonc`:

```jsonc
{
  "skills": {
    "paths": [".cursor/skills"]
  },
  "instructions": [
    ".kilo/rules/*.md",
    "AGENTS.md"
  ],
  "permission": {
    "bash": "ask",
    "read": "allow",
    "edit": "allow"
  }
}
```

That lets **both tools** share skills via `.cursor/skills`, while rules are duplicated or symlinked into `.kilo/rules/`.

---

## 6. What does *not* carry over

- **Cursor chat history** — archive/export only; no official import into Kilo
- **Cursor Team Rules / dashboard rules** — manual rewrite into `AGENTS.md` or `.kilo/rules/`
- **`.mdc` glob conditioning** — no 1:1 equivalent; use separate instruction files or custom agents
- **Cursor-only features** — Bugbot, Cloud Agents API, `/worktree`, etc. have different Kilo equivalents

---

## Practical migration order

1. Install Kilo Code extension + CLI; authenticate (`/connect` or `kilo auth login`).
2. Add `kilo.jsonc` with `skills.paths: [".cursor/skills"]`.
3. Convert `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` → `.kilo/rules/*.md`; register in `instructions`.
4. Add root `AGENTS.md` with the rules you want in *any* AI tool.
5. Migrate MCP from `.cursor/mcp.json` → `kilo.jsonc` `mcp` block.
6. Smoke-test: ponytail behavior, garden-voice on a note, deploy-commits guidance.

If you want, I can switch to Agent mode and scaffold `kilo.jsonc`, `AGENTS.md`, and the `.kilo/rules/` conversions for this repo without duplicating the skill files.

---

_**Agent (auto-low)**_

Implemented shared Cursor/Kilo agent config with **no symlinks and no duplicate trees**.

## Architecture

`.cursor/` is the **only** source of truth:

| Content | Path | Kilo loads via |
|---------|------|----------------|
| Rules | `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` | `kilo.jsonc` → `instructions` |
| Skills | `.cursor/skills/*/SKILL.md` | `kilo.jsonc` → `skills.paths` |

`AGENTS.md` is a short index only (no duplicated rule/skill bodies). `kilo.jsonc` points Kilo at the Cursor paths.

## New files

- **`kilo.jsonc`** — Kilo config reading `.cursor/skills` and `.cursor/rules/*.mdc`
- **`AGENTS.md`** — portable index + workflow reminders
- **`.cursor/rules/agent-config-sync.mdc`** — always-on rule: one tree, run lint, no `.kilo/` copies
- **`scripts/lint-agent-config.mjs`** — validates sync contract

## Lint commands

```bash
pnpm lint:agent-config   # full check (17 skills, 8 rules — passes)
pnpm test:agent-config   # self-check
```

The lint fails if:
- `kilo.jsonc` paths drift from `.cursor/`
- duplicate trees appear (`.kilo/skills`, `.kilocode/`, `.agents/skills`, etc.)
- skills lack valid `SKILL.md` frontmatter
- `AGENTS.md` drops canonical path references

## Kilo setup

Install Kilo Code, open this repo, start a new session (or `/reload`). Kilo should pick up all 17 skills and 8 rules from `.cursor/` automatically.

Also updated `deploy-commits.mdc` so `AGENTS.md` and `kilo.jsonc` count as tooling-only (`[skip ci]`).

## Session close
- Fixed: Kilo Code reads the same `.cursor/` rules and skills as Cursor via `kilo.jsonc`, with `pnpm lint:agent-config` enforcing sync
- Encode: none
- Open: clean
